newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Punjab provincial assembly dissolved.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Punjab provincial assembly dissolved.

text.p: The governor of Punjab, Pakistan's richest and most populous province, dissolved the provincial assembly on Sunday after the chief minister quit.

A government notification said Governor Tariq Rahim had dismissed the 248-seat assembly, bringing it into line with the other three provincial assemblies disbanded earlier, and appointed a new caretaker chief minister, Mohammad Afzal Hayat.

The dissolution of the Punjab assembly had been delayed by a tussle for power that was resolved when chief minister Manzoor Wattoo, who had been reinstated by a court on November 2, resigned earlier on Saturday, unable to win a confidence vote.

The assemblies in Baluchistan, Sindh and North West Frontier provinces were dissolved after President Farooq Leghari sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government and dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) on November 5.
Leghari, who said Bhutto's government had been paralysed by corruption and misrule, appointed Meraj Khalid as caretaker prime minister to supervise elections set for February 3.
Provincial assembly elections would normally take place soon after a general election.
"I do not want to be an obstacle in the election process. Neither do I want to cling to power," Wattoo said in his resignation letter to the Punjab governor.
"I hope this decision will be in the greater interest of the nation and will pave the way for free and fair elections."
Sunday's events were part of complex political manoeuvring in Punjab.

The Lahore High Court reinstated Wattoo on November 2 to the chagrin of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), which had engineered the chief minister's removal from power last year after a party revolt against him.

Wattoo represented a breakaway faction of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML), the main opposition to the PPP. Once a Sharif loyalist, he changed sides to enable the PPP to take control of Punjab, but the PPP later turned against him.
The Lahore High Court had told Wattoo to show that he commanded a majority in the assembly, failing which his outgoing rival Arif Nakai would be automatically reinstated.

The PPP had tabled a no-confidence motion against Wattoo, but withdrew it earlier on Saturday in an apparent attempt to prolong the life of the doomed assembly. The PML opposed the withdrawal of the no-confidence motion, but were outvoted.
Wattoo was due to have sought a vote of confidence on Sunday, but faced certain defeat given the PPP's hostility and the absence of 98 PML deputies who resigned on Saturday.
